title: SQL Create Table Standard
content:
-- Standard ANSI SQL CREATE TABLE
CREATE TABLE employees (                               -- naya table banao
    id         INTEGER      PRIMARY KEY,               -- unique identifier — duplicate nahi ho sakta
    first_name VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL,                  -- empty nahi ho sakta
    last_name  VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL,                  -- empty nahi ho sakta
    email      VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE,                    -- duplicate values allowed nahi
    salary     NUMERIC(10,2),
    dept_id    INTEGER      REFERENCES departments(id),
    hire_date  DATE         DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE,      -- agar value na di to yeh use hogi
    is_active  BOOLEAN      DEFAULT TRUE               -- agar value na di to yeh use hogi
);

-- View structure
SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable             -- data fetch karo
FROM information_schema.columns                        -- kis table se
WHERE table_name = 'employees';                        -- condition lagao

-- Alter: add column
ALTER TABLE employees ADD COLUMN phone VARCHAR(20);    -- table modify karo

-- Drop column
ALTER TABLE employees DROP COLUMN phone;               -- table modify karo

-- Drop table safely
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS employees CASCADE;                -- table delete karo

title: SQL Select Statement
content:
-- Select all columns
SELECT * FROM employees;                               -- data fetch karo

-- Select specific columns
SELECT first_name, last_name, salary FROM employees;   -- data fetch karo

-- Column aliases
SELECT first_name AS name, salary AS monthly_pay FROM employees; -- data fetch karo

-- Calculated column
SELECT first_name, salary,                             -- data fetch karo
    salary * 12 AS annual_salary                       -- alias naam do
FROM employees;                                        -- kis table se

-- Distinct values
SELECT DISTINCT dept_id FROM employees;                -- data fetch karo

-- Null handling
SELECT first_name, COALESCE(phone, 'N/A') AS contact FROM employees; -- data fetch karo

title: SQL Where Clause
content:
-- Basic condition
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 50000;          -- data fetch karo

-- AND condition
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 50000 AND is_active = TRUE; -- data fetch karo

-- OR condition
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1 OR dept_id = 2; -- data fetch karo

-- NOT condition
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE NOT is_active = FALSE;   -- data fetch karo

-- BETWEEN range
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary BETWEEN 40000 AND 80000; -- data fetch karo

-- LIKE pattern
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE first_name LIKE 'A%';     -- starts with A
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE email LIKE '%@gmail.com'; -- Gmail users

-- IN list
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE dept_id IN (1, 2, 3);    -- data fetch karo

-- IS NULL
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE email IS NULL;           -- data fetch karo
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE email IS NOT NULL;       -- data fetch karo

title: SQL Order By and Limit
content:
-- Sort ascending
SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY salary ASC;           -- data fetch karo

-- Sort descending (highest salary first)
SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC;          -- data fetch karo

-- Sort by multiple columns
SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY dept_id ASC, salary DESC; -- data fetch karo

-- Limit results (PostgreSQL / SQLite)
SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 10; -- data fetch karo

-- Pagination: page 2
SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 10 OFFSET 10; -- data fetch karo

-- SQL Server syntax (FETCH NEXT)
SELECT * FROM employees                                -- data fetch karo
ORDER BY salary DESC                                   -- sort karo
OFFSET 10 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY;                -- skip karo

title: SQL Group By and Aggregate Functions
content:
-- Count employees per department
SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS headcount                  -- data fetch karo
FROM employees                                         -- kis table se
GROUP BY dept_id;                                      -- group banao

-- Multiple aggregates
SELECT dept_id,                                        -- data fetch karo
    COUNT(*)        AS headcount,                      -- rows count karo
    AVG(salary)     AS avg_salary,                     -- average nikalo
    SUM(salary)     AS total_payroll,                  -- total nikalo
    MAX(salary)     AS highest_salary,                 -- maximum value
    MIN(salary)     AS lowest_salary                   -- minimum value
FROM employees                                         -- kis table se
GROUP BY dept_id;                                      -- group banao

-- HAVING: filter groups (departments with > 5 employees)
SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS headcount                  -- data fetch karo
FROM employees                                         -- kis table se
GROUP BY dept_id                                       -- group banao
HAVING COUNT(*) > 5                                    -- group filter karo
ORDER BY headcount DESC;                               -- sort karo

-- NOTE: WHERE filters rows BEFORE grouping
-- HAVING filters groups AFTER grouping

title: SQL Insert Data
content:

VALUES ('Alice', 'Smith', 75000, '2023-01-15');        -- jo values insert karni hain

    ('Bob',     'Jones',  65000),
    ('Charlie', 'Brown',  58000),
    ('Diana',   'Prince', 82000);

-- PostgreSQL UPSERT (ON CONFLICT)

VALUES (1, 'Alice', 80000)                             -- jo values insert karni hain
ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE
    SET salary = EXCLUDED.salary;                      -- naya value set karo

title: SQL Update
content:
-- Update single field
UPDATE employees SET salary = 80000 WHERE id = 1;      -- condition lagao

-- Update multiple fields
UPDATE employees                                       -- data update karo
SET salary = 85000, is_active = TRUE                   -- naya value set karo
WHERE email = 'alice@company.com';                     -- condition lagao

-- Increase salary by 10% for a department
UPDATE employees                                       -- data update karo
SET salary = salary * 1.10                             -- naya value set karo
WHERE dept_id = 3;                                     -- condition lagao

-- Conditional update with CASE
UPDATE employees                                       -- data update karo
SET grade = CASE                                       -- naya value set karo
    WHEN salary > 100000 THEN 'Senior'
    WHEN salary > 60000  THEN 'Mid'
    ELSE 'Junior'
END;

-- Update from another table (SQL standard)
UPDATE employees e                                     -- data update karo
SET salary = e.salary * 1.05                           -- naya value set karo
WHERE e.dept_id IN (                                   -- condition lagao
    SELECT id FROM departments WHERE performance_score > 90 -- data fetch karo
);

title: SQL Delete
content:
-- Delete specific row

-- Delete with condition

-- Delete using subquery

WHERE id IN (                                          -- condition lagao
    SELECT emp_id FROM performance WHERE rating < 2    -- data fetch karo
);

title: SQL Inner Join
content:
-- INNER JOIN: returns only rows where there is a MATCH in BOTH tables
-- If a row in left table has no match in right table, it is EXCLUDED

-- Basic INNER JOIN: students with their courses
SELECT
    s.name         AS student_name,   -- column from students table (alias s)
    s.marks,                          -- marks from students
    c.course_name                     -- column from courses table (alias c)
FROM students s                       -- 's' is alias for students table
INNER JOIN enrollments e              -- join through bridge table
    ON s.id = e.student_id            -- connection: student id must match
INNER JOIN courses c                  -- join to courses table
    ON e.course_id = c.id;            -- connection: course id must match

-- Only students who ARE enrolled and the course EXISTS appear
-- Unenrolled students are EXCLUDED (that's what INNER means)

-- With WHERE filter: only top-performing enrolled students
SELECT s.name, s.marks, c.course_name                  -- data fetch karo
FROM students s                                        -- kis table se
INNER JOIN enrollments e ON s.id = e.student_id        -- tables jodo
INNER JOIN courses c     ON e.course_id = c.id         -- tables jodo
WHERE s.marks > 75          -- apply filter AFTER joining
ORDER BY s.marks DESC;      -- sort highest marks first

title: SQL Left Right Full Outer Join
content:
-- LEFT JOIN: all rows from left table + matching from right
-- (NULL for right side where no match)
SELECT e.first_name, d.name AS dept                    -- data fetch karo
FROM employees e                                       -- kis table se
LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;           -- tables jodo

-- RIGHT JOIN: all rows from right table + matching from left
SELECT e.first_name, d.name AS dept                    -- data fetch karo
FROM employees e                                       -- kis table se
RIGHT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;          -- tables jodo

-- FULL OUTER JOIN: all rows from both tables
SELECT e.first_name, d.name AS dept                    -- data fetch karo
FROM employees e                                       -- kis table se
FULL OUTER JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;     -- tables jodo

-- Self JOIN: employee with their manager
SELECT e.first_name AS employee, m.first_name AS manager -- data fetch karo
FROM employees e                                       -- kis table se
LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id;          -- tables jodo

-- CROSS JOIN: every combination
SELECT s.size, c.color                                 -- data fetch karo
FROM sizes s CROSS JOIN colors c;                      -- kis table se

title: SQL Subquery
content:
-- Subquery in WHERE
SELECT first_name, salary FROM employees               -- data fetch karo
WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);    -- data fetch karo

-- Subquery with IN
SELECT first_name FROM employees                       -- data fetch karo
WHERE dept_id IN (SELECT id FROM departments WHERE location = 'NY'); -- data fetch karo

-- EXISTS subquery
SELECT first_name FROM employees e                     -- data fetch karo
WHERE EXISTS (                                         -- condition lagao
    SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.emp_id = e.id       -- data fetch karo
);

-- Correlated subquery
SELECT e.first_name, e.salary,                         -- data fetch karo
    (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees WHERE dept_id = e.dept_id) AS dept_avg -- data fetch karo
FROM employees e;                                      -- kis table se

-- Subquery in FROM (derived table)
SELECT dept_id, avg_sal FROM (                         -- data fetch karo
    SELECT dept_id, AVG(salary) AS avg_sal             -- data fetch karo
    FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id                    -- kis table se
) AS dept_averages                                     -- alias naam do
WHERE avg_sal > 60000;                                 -- condition lagao

title: SQL CTE With Clause
content:
-- CTE (Common Table Expression): temporary named result set
-- Defined with WITH keyword, exists only for the duration of the query
-- Makes complex queries more readable (like creating a temporary view)

-- ── Simple CTE ────────────────────────────────────────────────
WITH high_earners AS (
    -- This is the CTE definition — like a temporary table
    SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 80000  -- filter for high earners
)
-- Main query uses the CTE like a regular table
SELECT * FROM high_earners                             -- data fetch karo
WHERE dept_id = 1;  -- can add more filters to the CTE result

-- ── Multiple CTEs (separate with commas) ──────────────────────
WITH
dept_avg AS (
    SELECT dept_id, AVG(salary) AS avg_sal   -- average salary per dept
    FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id                    -- kis table se
),
above_avg AS (
    SELECT e.first_name, e.salary, d.avg_sal  -- employees earning above their dept avg
    FROM employees e                                   -- kis table se
    JOIN dept_avg d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id           -- tables jodo
    WHERE e.salary > d.avg_sal               -- compare with department average
)
SELECT * FROM above_avg ORDER BY salary DESC;  -- use second CTE in main query

-- ── Recursive CTE (hierarchical data like org charts) ─────────
WITH RECURSIVE org_chart AS (
    -- Base case: start with top-level managers (no manager_id)
    SELECT id, first_name, manager_id, 0 AS level      -- data fetch karo
    FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL            -- kis table se

    UNION ALL   -- combine base case with recursive case

    -- Recursive case: find employees of each manager
    SELECT e.id, e.first_name, e.manager_id, oc.level + 1  -- increment level
    FROM employees e                                   -- kis table se
    JOIN org_chart oc ON e.manager_id = oc.id  -- connect to previous level
)
SELECT * FROM org_chart ORDER BY level;  -- show hierarchy from top down

title: SQL Window Functions
content:
-- Window functions compute value ACROSS related rows WITHOUT collapsing them
-- Unlike GROUP BY, each row keeps its identity

-- ROW_NUMBER: assigns sequential number within each partition
SELECT name, salary, dept_id,                          -- data fetch karo
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY dept_id    -- restart numbering for each department
        ORDER BY salary DESC    -- highest salary gets row number 1
    ) AS row_num                                       -- alias naam do
FROM employees;                                        -- kis table se

-- RANK: like ROW_NUMBER but ties get same rank (gaps after ties: 1,1,3)
SELECT name, salary,                                   -- data fetch karo
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank  -- sort karo
FROM employees;                                        -- kis table se

-- DENSE_RANK: like RANK but no gaps (1,1,2 — not 1,1,3)
SELECT name, salary,                                   -- data fetch karo
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS dense_rank -- sort karo
FROM employees;                                        -- kis table se

-- LAG: access value from PREVIOUS row (salary change analysis)
SELECT name, salary,                                   -- data fetch karo
    LAG(salary) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) AS prev_salary,      -- previous row's salary
    salary - LAG(salary) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) AS change   -- salary increase/decrease
FROM employees;                                        -- kis table se

-- LEAD: access value from NEXT row
SELECT name, salary,                                   -- data fetch karo
    LEAD(salary) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) AS next_salary -- sort karo
FROM employees;                                        -- kis table se

-- Running total (cumulative sum)
SELECT name, salary,                                   -- data fetch karo
    SUM(salary) OVER (                                 -- total nikalo
        ORDER BY hire_date                             -- sort karo
        ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING   -- sum from first row to current row
    ) AS running_total                                 -- alias naam do
FROM employees;                                        -- kis table se

title: SQL Union Intersect Except
content:
-- UNION: combine results, remove duplicates
SELECT name FROM employees                             -- data fetch karo
UNION
SELECT name FROM contractors;                          -- data fetch karo

-- UNION ALL: combine results, keep duplicates (faster)
SELECT email FROM employees                            -- data fetch karo
UNION ALL
SELECT email FROM contractors;                         -- data fetch karo

-- INTERSECT: rows that exist in BOTH queries
SELECT email FROM employees                            -- data fetch karo
INTERSECT
SELECT email FROM customers;                           -- data fetch karo

-- EXCEPT (MINUS in Oracle): in first but NOT in second
SELECT email FROM employees                            -- data fetch karo
EXCEPT
SELECT email FROM unsubscribed;                        -- data fetch karo

-- NOTE: MySQL does not support INTERSECT/EXCEPT natively
-- Use subquery instead:
SELECT email FROM employees                            -- data fetch karo
WHERE email IN (SELECT email FROM customers);  -- MySQL INTERSECT alternative

SELECT email FROM employees                            -- data fetch karo
WHERE email NOT IN (SELECT email FROM unsubscribed);  -- MySQL EXCEPT alternative

title: SQL Case Expression
content:
-- CASE expression: conditional logic inside SQL queries
-- Like if-else but for column values

-- ── Searched CASE (most flexible) ────────────────────────────
SELECT
    first_name,
    salary,
    CASE
        WHEN salary > 100000 THEN 'Senior'    -- if salary > 100000
        WHEN salary > 60000  THEN 'Mid'       -- else if salary > 60000
        WHEN salary > 40000  THEN 'Junior'    -- else if salary > 40000
        ELSE                      'Entry'     -- none of the above
    END AS level                              -- column alias for the result
FROM employees;                                        -- kis table se

-- ── Simple CASE (like switch statement) ──────────────────────
SELECT
    first_name,
    CASE dept_id            -- evaluate dept_id once
        WHEN 1 THEN 'Engineering'   -- when equals 1
        WHEN 2 THEN 'Marketing'     -- when equals 2
        WHEN 3 THEN 'Sales'         -- when equals 3
        ELSE       'Other'          -- for any other value
    END AS department_name                             -- alias naam do
FROM employees;                                        -- kis table se

-- ── CASE in WHERE clause ──────────────────────────────────────
SELECT * FROM employees                                -- data fetch karo
WHERE CASE                                             -- condition lagao
    WHEN dept_id = 1 THEN salary > 80000   -- Engineering: high threshold
    ELSE                   salary > 50000  -- Other depts: lower threshold
END;

-- ── CASE in aggregate (conditional count) ────────────────────
SELECT
    COUNT(CASE WHEN salary > 80000 THEN 1 END) AS high_earners,  -- count seniors
    COUNT(CASE WHEN salary <= 80000 THEN 1 END) AS others,        -- count others
    COUNT(*) AS total                                               -- total employees
FROM employees;                                        -- kis table se

title: SQL Create View
content:
-- Create a simple view
CREATE VIEW active_employees AS                        -- virtual table banao
SELECT e.id, e.first_name, e.last_name, e.salary, d.name AS department -- data fetch karo
FROM employees e                                       -- kis table se
JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id                 -- tables jodo
WHERE e.is_active = TRUE;                              -- condition lagao

-- Use view like a table
SELECT * FROM active_employees WHERE salary > 70000;   -- data fetch karo

-- Update view data (if updatable)
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW active_employees AS
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE is_active = TRUE;        -- data fetch karo

-- Drop view
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS active_employees;

-- Materialized View (PostgreSQL only - stores actual data)
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW dept_summary AS
SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS emp_count, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary -- data fetch karo
FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id;                       -- kis table se

-- Refresh materialized view
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW dept_summary;

title: SQL Create Index
content:
-- Single column index
CREATE INDEX idx_emp_email ON employees(email);        -- search fast karne ke liye

-- Unique index (enforces no duplicates)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_email_unique ON employees(email); -- duplicate values allowed nahi

-- Composite index (queries filtering dept + salary)
CREATE INDEX idx_dept_salary ON employees(dept_id, salary DESC); -- search fast karne ke liye

-- Partial index (PostgreSQL): only index active employees
CREATE INDEX idx_active_emp ON employees(last_name)    -- search fast karne ke liye
WHERE is_active = TRUE;                                -- condition lagao

-- Drop index
DROP INDEX idx_emp_email;                              -- search fast karne ke liye

-- Check query execution plan
EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM employees WHERE email = 'alice@company.com'; -- data fetch karo

-- TIPS:
-- Add indexes on columns you frequently use in WHERE, JOIN, ORDER BY
-- Too many indexes slow down INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
-- Use EXPLAIN to check if your query actually uses the index

title: SQL Transaction ACID
content:
-- Start transaction
BEGIN;

  -- Transfer ₹500 from account 1 to account 2
  UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 500 WHERE id = 1; -- condition lagao
  UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 500 WHERE id = 2; -- condition lagao

COMMIT;  -- Make changes permanent

-- Rollback on error
BEGIN;
  UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 500 WHERE id = 1; -- condition lagao
ROLLBACK;  -- Undo everything since BEGIN

-- Savepoint: partial rollback
BEGIN;
  INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, 'Order A', 1000);      -- data add karo
  SAVEPOINT after_order;
  INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (1, 'Item X', 500);  -- risky operation
  ROLLBACK TO after_order;  -- undo only the item insert
COMMIT;                                                -- changes save karo

-- Add constraint to table
ALTER TABLE employees                                  -- table modify karo
ADD CONSTRAINT chk_salary CHECK (salary > 0);          -- value validation lagao

-- ACID: Atomicity (all or nothing), Consistency, Isolation, Durability

title: SQL Constraints
content:
CREATE TABLE students (                                -- naya table banao
    id         INTEGER      PRIMARY KEY,           -- must be unique, not null
    name       VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,              -- cannot be empty
    email      VARCHAR(150) UNIQUE,                -- no duplicates
    age        INTEGER      CHECK (age > 0 AND age < 120), -- valid range
    class      VARCHAR(20)  DEFAULT '10th',        -- default value
    dept_id    INTEGER      REFERENCES departments(id)  -- foreign key
);

-- Named constraints (easier to drop/manage)
CREATE TABLE orders (                                  -- naya table banao
    id         INTEGER,
    amount     NUMERIC(10,2),
    customer_id INTEGER,
    CONSTRAINT pk_orders PRIMARY KEY (id),             -- unique identifier — duplicate nahi ho sakta
    CONSTRAINT chk_amount CHECK (amount > 0),          -- value validation lagao
    CONSTRAINT fk_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_id)   -- doosre table se link karo
        REFERENCES customers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

-- Add constraint after table creation
ALTER TABLE students                                   -- table modify karo
ADD CONSTRAINT chk_marks CHECK (marks >= 0 AND marks <= 100); -- value validation lagao

title: SQL Create Table Students
content:

title: SQL Create Table Products
content:

title: SQL Having Clause
content:
-- HAVING filters GROUPS after GROUP BY
-- WHERE filters ROWS before grouping
-- Key difference: WHERE cannot use aggregate functions, HAVING can

-- Example 1: Departments with more than 3 employees
SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS emp_count    -- count employees per dept
FROM employees                                         -- kis table se
GROUP BY department                          -- group into departments
HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;                        -- keep only groups with 4+ employees

-- Example 2: Classes where average marks exceed 80
SELECT class,                                          -- data fetch karo
    COUNT(*) AS students,                    -- number of students
    ROUND(AVG(marks), 2) AS avg_marks       -- average marks (2 decimal places)
FROM students                                          -- kis table se
GROUP BY class                               -- group by class
HAVING AVG(marks) > 80                      -- filter: only classes with avg > 80
ORDER BY avg_marks DESC;                    -- sort by average descending

-- Example 3: Product categories with total inventory value > 100000
SELECT
    category,
    COUNT(*)               AS products,     -- number of products
    SUM(price * quantity)  AS total_value   -- total stock value
FROM products                                          -- kis table se
GROUP BY category                                      -- group banao
HAVING SUM(price * quantity) > 100000;     -- only high-value categories

title: SQL Stored Functions
SQL Trigger
content:
-- Create audit table
CREATE TABLE audit_log (                               -- naya table banao
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,                    -- unique identifier — duplicate nahi ho sakta
    table_name VARCHAR(50),
    action     VARCHAR(20),
    record_id  INTEGER,
    changed_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP     -- agar value na di to yeh use hogi
);

-- PostgreSQL trigger function
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION log_student_change()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN                                                  -- transaction shuru karo
    INSERT INTO audit_log (table_name, action, record_id) -- data add karo
    VALUES ('students', TG_OP, NEW.id);                -- jo values insert karni hain
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- Attach trigger
CREATE TRIGGER after_student_insert
AFTER INSERT ON students
FOR EACH ROW
EXECUTE FUNCTION log_student_change();

-- Test
INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Test', 80); -- data add karo
SELECT * FROM audit_log;                               -- data fetch karo

title: SQL Pivot and Crosstab
content:
-- Conditional aggregation (manual pivot)
SELECT
    student_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN subject = 'Math'     THEN marks END) AS math, -- maximum value
    MAX(CASE WHEN subject = 'Science'  THEN marks END) AS science, -- maximum value
    MAX(CASE WHEN subject = 'English'  THEN marks END) AS english, -- maximum value
    ROUND(AVG(marks), 2)                               AS overall_avg -- average nikalo
FROM exam_results                                      -- kis table se
GROUP BY student_id                                    -- group banao
ORDER BY overall_avg DESC;                             -- sort karo

-- Count by status in columns
SELECT
    department,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'active')   AS active, -- condition lagao
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'inactive') AS inactive, -- condition lagao
    COUNT(*) AS total                                  -- rows count karo
FROM employees                                         -- kis table se
GROUP BY department;                                   -- group banao
